षण्ड: Ṣaṇḍa is the name of a priest at the snake festival described in the Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa.^1 Cf. Kuṣaṇḍa. 1) xxv. 15, 3. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 35.
षण्डिक: Ṣaṇḍika is mentioned in the Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā^1 as a con-temporary of Keśin. Probably Khaṇḍika should be read as usual elsewhere. 1) i. 4, 12, where von Schroeder gives no variant. But ṣ and kh are constantly interchanged in manuscripts.
